html:
The Battle of Hattin was fought on 4 July 1187 near the Horns of Hattin, a hill above the Sea of Galilee in today's northern Israel. Saladin destroyed the army of the crusader Kingdom of Jerusalem.

Saladin had united Egypt and Syria and surrounded the crusader states. When the lord Raynald of Châtillon attacked a Muslim caravan during a truce, Saladin had his cause for war. He besieged Tiberias to draw the crusaders out. King Guy of Lusignan gathered almost every fighting man in the kingdom, about 20,000, and marched to relieve it across dry hills in midsummer. Saladin's horse archers harassed the column all day and kept it from water. The crusaders spent the night thirsty, with the enemy burning dry grass upwind of them. The next day the infantry broke and climbed the Horns, and the knights' charges failed. Almost the whole army was killed or captured. Saladin spared Guy and killed Raynald himself.

With no army left, the kingdom's towns fell one after another. Jerusalem, held since the First Crusade, surrendered on 2 October. The news set off the Third Crusade, which won back the coast but not the city.
